sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java Concurrency and Multithreading interview questions are where senior interviews are won or lost. This page covers threads and the Thread lifecycle, the Java Memory Model (happens-before, volatile vs synchronized), synchronization and locks, the ExecutorService and thread pools, CompletableFuture, concurrent collections (ConcurrentHashMap internals), virtual threads (Java 21+ Project Loom), and the patterns interviewers actually ask about (producer-consumer, CountDownLatch vs CyclicBarrier vs Semaphore). Every answer leads with the conceptual model, then the API, then the failure mode that distinguishes a 3-year engineer from a 10-year one.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three layers — and you must name them in order:

1. **Memory model** — happens-before, `volatile`, `synchronized`, final-field freeze.
2. **Synchronisers** — locks (`ReentrantLock`), latches, semaphores, barriers, `StampedLock`.
3. **Executors** — `ExecutorService`, `ForkJoinPool`, `CompletableFuture`, virtual threads.

Pick the **lowest level** that solves your problem; senior interviewers reward `CompletableFuture` over raw threads, and an executor over `new Thread(...)`.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **`synchronized` vs `ReentrantLock`** — Lock gives `tryLock`, fairness, multiple conditions; mention each.
- **Double-checked locking** — broken pre-Java 5 without `volatile`; quote it as a memory-model interview classic.
- **`ConcurrentHashMap`** — lock striping in 7, CAS-based bins in 8+.
- **Virtual threads** — cheap, scheduled on carrier threads; *avoid* `synchronized` blocks on hot paths (pinning).
- **Producer-consumer** — `BlockingQueue` is the canonical Java answer; mention `LinkedBlockingQueue` vs `ArrayBlockingQueue` (bounded vs unbounded).

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"The contention is on <shared resource>. I'd guard it with <synchronized | ReentrantLock | atomic | concurrent collection> because <reason: granularity / fairness / read-heavy>. For the wider workflow I'd compose it with `CompletableFuture` so the I/O is non-blocking, and I'd watch <thread-pool starvation | pinning under virtual threads>."*
